title: Kingdom of Bernicia
capsule: Bernicia was an Anglian kingdom stretching from the Firth of Forth to the River Tees along the northeast coast of Britain, with its chief stronghold at Bamburgh; the first recorded king, Ida, obtained the throne around 547. Under Æthelfrith (r. c. 593–616) Bernicia was united with neighboring Deira by conquest around 604, creating the precursor of Northumbria. Oswald of Bernicia (r. 634–642), returning from Irish exile at Iona, defeated the Welsh king Cadwallon at Heavenfield in 634, invited Aidan to found Lindisfarne monastery, and established Northumbrian Christian kingship; his brother Oswiu then permanently unified Bernicia and Deira under the Northumbrian crown.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Bernicia's core territory in Northumberland is identified through Bede's Ecclesiastical History and place-name evidence; its northern extent into Scotland and its precise frontier with Deira are reconstructed from narrative and archaeological sources with limited precision.
